lewis-diagrams-s2.title: Valence electron counts
lewis-diagrams-s2.text: A student records the valence electrons for several species before drawing their Lewis diagrams.

items.q: Which diagram shows the wrong total number of valence electrons for its formula?
options: Diagram 1
Diagram 3
Diagram 2
Diagram 4

why.correct: N₂ has 2 × 5 = 10 valence electrons. Diagram 3 shows a double bond (4) and four lone pairs (8), which is 12. The correct diagram is a triple bond with one lone pair on each N: 6 + 4 = 10.
options: HCN has 1 + 4 + 5 = 10: one single bond (2), a triple bond (6) and one lone pair (2). It is correct.
Right: 12 electrons drawn for a 10-electron molecule.
H₂CO has 2 + 4 + 6 = 12: two C–H bonds (4), a C=O bond (4) and two lone pairs (4). It is correct.
BF₃ has 3 + 21 = 24: three bonds (6) and nine lone pairs (18). It is correct, with an incomplete octet on B.

items.q: In Diagram 4, how many electrons surround the boron atom, and what does this show?
options: Ten, an expanded octet, because B is in period 2
Eight, because each atom in a molecule has an octet
Six, so the diagram has to be wrong
Six, an incomplete octet, which boron can have

why.correct: B has three bonds and no lone pairs: 3 × 2 = 6 electrons. Boron has only three valence electrons, so in BF₃ it ends with six, an incomplete octet. This is one of the known exceptions to the octet rule.
options: Period 2 atoms such as B cannot have more than eight electrons; expanded octets start in period 3.
Not every atom has an octet: H has 2, and B commonly has 6.
Six around B is allowed; the diagram uses exactly 24 electrons and each F has an octet.
Right: three bonding pairs, six electrons.

items.q: In Diagram 2 (H₂CO), how many lone pairs are on the whole molecule?

why.correct: Only O carries lone pairs: two of them. C has four bonding pairs (two to H and a double bond to O) and no lone pairs.

items.q: How does the C atom in Diagram 1 (HCN) reach an octet?
options: A single bond to H and a triple bond to N: 2 + 6 = 8
It has two lone pairs plus two single bonds to H and N
It has one lone pair, a single bond and a double bond
It does not reach an octet; carbon has an incomplete octet in HCN

why.correct: Count every bonding electron around C: H–C contributes 2 and C≡N contributes 6. 2 + 6 = 8, an octet, with no lone pairs on C.
options: Right: two bonding electrons plus six.
The diagram shows no lone pairs on C and a triple bond to N.
The C–N bond is triple, not double, and C has no lone pair.
C has eight electrons around it; incomplete octets are typical of B, not C.

items.q: How many valence electrons must the Lewis diagram of the sulfate ion, SO₄²⁻, show?

mistakes.why: Value: you left out the charge. A 2− charge means two extra electrons: add 2 to the atoms' 30.
Value: you subtracted 2 for the charge. A 2− ion has gained two electrons: add 2.

why.correct: S 6 + 4 × O 6 = 30, plus 2 for the 2− charge = 32 electrons.

items.q: How many valence electrons must the Lewis diagram of the borohydride ion, BH₄⁻, show?

mistakes.why: Value: you subtracted an electron for the 1− charge. A negative ion has gained an electron: add 1.

why.correct: B 3 + 4 × H 1 = 7, plus 1 for the 1− charge = 8 electrons. Four B–H bonds use all 8, giving B an octet.

items.q: Which species in the table cannot have every atom with an octet in its Lewis diagram?
options: BH₄⁻
PCl₃
NO
SO₄²⁻

why.correct: NO has 5 + 6 = 11 valence electrons, an odd number. Electrons in a Lewis diagram come in pairs, so one electron is left unpaired and one atom has fewer than eight. NO is an odd-electron species (a free radical).
options: BH₄⁻ has 8 electrons: four B–H bonds give B an octet, and each H has its 2.
PCl₃ has 26 electrons: three P–Cl bonds, a lone pair on P and three on each Cl gives every atom an octet.
Right: an odd total cannot be all pairs.
SO₄²⁻ has 32 electrons and can be drawn with an octet on every atom (four S–O single bonds).

items.q: In SF₆, sulfur forms six bonds. Which statement is correct?
options: SF₆ is not a real compound, as S would break the octet rule
S has 8 electrons, because each bond counts as one electron for S
S has 12 electrons, an expanded octet, possible in period 3
S has 12 electrons, and each F has an expanded octet too

why.correct: Six bonding pairs put 12 electrons around S. Atoms in period 3 and below can hold more than eight valence electrons (an expanded octet). Each F has one bond and three lone pairs: an ordinary octet.
options: SF₆ is a real, stable gas; period 3 atoms can exceed the octet.
Both electrons of a bonding pair count for each atom it joins.
Right: six bonds, 12 electrons, period 3.
Each F has exactly 8 (one bond, three lone pairs); F is in period 2 and cannot expand.

items.q: In a Lewis diagram, what does a lone pair represent?
options: Two valence electrons on one atom, not shared
Two electrons shared between two atoms in a bond
Two core electrons held close to the nucleus
A single unpaired electron on one atom

why.correct: A lone pair (nonbonding pair) is a pair of valence electrons that belongs to one atom and is not shared.
options: Right: an unshared pair of valence electrons.
Two shared electrons are a bonding pair, drawn as a line.
Lewis diagrams show valence electrons only; core electrons are left out.
An unpaired electron is a single dot, found in odd-electron species.

items.q: Put the steps for drawing a Lewis diagram in order.
options: Count the valence electrons, adjusting for any charge
Place the central atom and connect each outer atom with a single bond
Complete the octets of the outer atoms with lone pairs
Put any electrons left over on the central atom
If the central atom lacks an octet, turn outer lone pairs into double or triple bonds

why.correct: Count, skeleton, outer octets, leftovers on the center, then multiple bonds if the center is short. Check at the end that the diagram uses exactly the counted number of electrons.

items.q: What is the correct Lewis diagram for carbon dioxide, CO₂?
options: O≡C–O, with one lone pair on the triple-bonded O and two on the other
O–C–O, with three lone pairs on each O and no lone pair on C
O–C–O, with three lone pairs on each O and two on C
O=C=O, with two lone pairs on each O

why.correct: CO₂ has 4 + 2 × 6 = 16 electrons. Two double bonds (8) and two lone pairs on each O (8) use all 16, and every atom has an octet.
options: That uses 8 + 2 + 4 = 14 electrons and leaves the single-bonded O short of an octet.
That uses 4 + 12 = 16 electrons but leaves C with only four electrons; lone pairs on O must become double bonds.
That uses 4 + 12 + 4 = 20 electrons, four more than CO₂ has.
Right: 16 electrons, octets everywhere.

items.q: A student drew the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺, as N bonded to four H atoms with one lone pair on N. What is wrong?
options: It has too few electrons; N needs two lone pairs
It shows 10 electrons; NH₄⁺ has 8, so no lone pair
Nothing is wrong; N keeps its one lone pair
H atoms need lone pairs to complete their octets

why.correct: NH₄⁺ has 5 + 4 − 1 = 8 electrons. Four N–H bonds use all 8, so there is no lone pair. The student added an electron for the charge instead of removing one.
options: Two lone pairs would make the count even larger, 12 electrons.
Right: the 1+ charge removes an electron.
In NH₃ nitrogen has a lone pair, but in NH₄⁺ that pair has become the fourth N–H bond.
H holds two electrons, one bonding pair; it never needs eight.

items.q: Which of these molecules has a central atom with an expanded octet in its Lewis diagram? Select all that apply.
options: PCl₅
CCl₄
NF₃
BCl₃

why.correct: P in PCl₅ makes five bonds: 10 electrons around a period 3 atom. The others have eight or fewer around the central atom.
options: Right: five bonding pairs, 10 electrons.
C has four bonds, exactly an octet.
N has three bonds and a lone pair, exactly an octet; period 2 atoms cannot expand.
B has three bonds and no lone pair: six electrons, an incomplete octet, not an expanded one.

items.q: Draw the Lewis diagram of nitrogen trichloride, NCl₃. How many lone pairs does the whole molecule have?

mistakes.why: Value: you counted the chlorine lone pairs only. N also keeps one lone pair: 26 electrons − 6 in bonds = 20 = 10 pairs.

why.correct: Valence electrons: 5 + 3 × 7 = 26. Three N–Cl bonds use 6, leaving 20 electrons = 10 lone pairs: three on each Cl (9) and one on N.

items.q: Which is the correct skeleton (arrangement of atoms) for the hypochlorous acid molecule, HOCl?
options: H–Cl–O, with Cl as the central atom
H–O–Cl, with O as the central atom
O–H–Cl, with H as the central atom
Cl–O and H unbonded beside them

why.correct: H forms only one bond, so it sits on the outside. In acids that contain oxygen, the H is attached to an O, and O (which forms two bonds) links H to Cl. The skeleton is H–O–Cl.
options: In acids that contain oxygen, the H is bonded to O, and H–O–Cl gives every atom an octet without any charges.
Right: O in the middle, H on the end.
H holds two electrons, one bond, so it cannot be a central atom.
Every atom in a molecule is connected; an unbonded H would make it two separate species.

items.q: Which is the correct Lewis diagram for the cyanide ion, CN⁻?
options: [C–N]⁻ with three lone pairs on each atom
[C≡N]⁻ with no lone pairs on either atom
[C=N]⁻ with two lone pairs on each atom
[C≡N]⁻ with one lone pair on each atom

why.correct: CN⁻ has 4 + 5 + 1 = 10 electrons. A triple bond (6) and one lone pair on each atom (4) use 10, and both atoms have octets.
options: That uses 2 + 12 = 14 electrons, four more than the ion has.
That uses only 6 electrons and leaves both atoms short.
That uses 4 + 8 = 12 electrons, two more than the ion has.
Right: 10 electrons, two octets.
